title: Ремонтвижн — дизайн по фото с материалами и ценами
description: Примерьте ремонт до покупок: дизайн вашей комнаты по фото, реальные товары и смета. Две генерации бесплатно, без подписки.

inputs.value:
Edit the supplied room photo into an empty, unfurnished room.

This is a removal and local surface-restoration task only.
It is NOT a redesign, renovation, repainting or virtual staging task.

GOAL:
Remove furniture, decorative objects, electrical outlets, switches,
lighting fixtures and all visible traces of those removed items.
Preserve the existing room architecture and surface finishes.
The result must look like the same room, photographed from the same
position, but cleared of the objects listed below.

REMOVE — FURNITURE AND LOOSE OBJECTS:
- All freestanding furniture: sofas, armchairs, chairs, tables,
  beds, desks, dressers, freestanding wardrobes and storage units.
- Rugs, plants, planters, books, baskets, toys, appliances that
  are not integrated into cabinetry, and all other loose items.
- Cushions, blankets, bedding and other removable textiles.
- Curtains, drapes, blinds and their visible rods, tracks,
  brackets and mounting hardware.

REMOVE — WALL DECOR AND EQUIPMENT:
- Decorative mirrors, including framed and frameless mirrors.
- Artwork, paintings, posters, picture frames and wall clocks.
- Applied decorative wall panels that are separate mounted objects,
  not the underlying continuous wall finish.
- Televisions, display screens, TV brackets and visible cables.
- Decorative wall shelves, their contents and mounting hardware.
- Hooks, picture hangers and brackets belonging to removed objects.

REMOVE — ELECTRICAL DEVICES:
- All visible electrical outlets, sockets, switches and dimmers.
- Electrical faceplates, frames, data sockets and TV connection plates.
- Surface-mounted electrical boxes, cable covers and visible wiring.
- Remove these devices even when they are recessed into a wall,
  floor, ceiling or preserved cabinet.

REMOVE — LIGHTING:
- Chandeliers, pendant lights and ceiling-mounted fixtures.
- Wall sconces, spotlights, track lights and recessed downlights.
- Floor lamps, table lamps and visible decorative LED strips.
- All associated bulbs, shades, diffusers, ceiling canopies,
  mounting plates, tracks, brackets, suspension cords,
  chains, transformers and visible cables.

IMPORTANT — MIRRORS:
Remove each decorative mirror completely, including its reflective
glass, frame, reflected scene and visible mounting hardware.

A decorative mirror is an object to remove, not a window,
doorway, opening or architectural feature.

Replace its entire former area with a continuous, non-reflective
surface matching the immediately surrounding wall.

Do not replace mirrors with windows, doorways, artwork, niches,
wall panels or a different reflective surface.

Preserve actual windows, glass doors and mirrored doors that are
integral parts of preserved built-in cabinetry.

IMPORTANT — OUTLETS AND SWITCHES:
Remove the entire visible outlet or switch assembly.
Fill its former location with a seamless continuation of the
surrounding surface.

Do not leave holes, electrical boxes, faceplates, outlines,
dark patches, exposed wires or replacement cover plates.

IMPORTANT — LIGHTING FIXTURES:
Remove every fixture completely, including its attachment points.

For recessed lights, fill the openings with a seamless continuation
of the existing ceiling.
For track lights, remove the entire track and all attached components.
For pendant lights and chandeliers, remove the ceiling canopy,
suspension hardware and any visible ceiling hook.

Do not leave exposed wires, mounting holes, ceiling cups,
fixture silhouettes, bright rings or glowing outlines.

IMPORTANT — RESIDUAL ARTIFICIAL LIGHT:
Remove the lighting effects caused by the removed fixtures,
not just the physical fixtures themselves.

Remove:
- Localized bright spots and hotspots on the ceiling and walls.
- Glowing halos around former light positions.
- Reflected light patches and specular highlights caused by
  removed artificial lights.
- Radial light patterns, light cones and decorative light washes.
- Warm or cool localized color casts from removed fixtures.
- Bright rings, luminous outlines and fixture-shaped light traces.
- Shadows and reflections cast by removed objects.

Do not preserve a bright patch simply because it appears in
the source photograph. If it was caused by a removed fixture,
remove it together with that fixture.

Restore these areas using the surrounding surface material,
texture and base color, with plausible daylight illumination.

Preserve natural daylight from existing windows, including broad,
soft light gradients and genuine sunlight patterns.
Do not erase natural window light or flatten the entire ceiling
into a uniform white surface.

Where a light effect is ambiguous, remove clearly localized
fixture-shaped hotspots while retaining broad daylight gradients.

PRESERVE — ARCHITECTURE:
- Exact room geometry, dimensions, proportions and ceiling height.
- Original camera position, perspective, framing and aspect ratio.
- All existing walls, ceiling planes and floor levels.
- Windows, doors, door frames and architectural openings.
- Structural columns, beams, stairs and architectural trim.
- Baseboards, cornices and continuous architectural moldings.
- Radiators, heating pipes and ventilation grilles.
- Built-in kitchen units, sanitary fixtures and integrated cabinetry,
  unless explicitly requested otherwise.

PRESERVE — EXISTING FINISHES:
- Existing wall, ceiling and floor materials.
- Existing paint colors, wallpaper, plaster texture and tile patterns.
- Existing wood grain, flooring direction, joints and grout lines.
- Existing architectural paneling and continuous wall cladding.
- Surface wear and irregularities unrelated to removed objects.

Do not globally repaint, smooth, recolor or replace these finishes.
Only reconstruct the local areas revealed by removed objects
and remove the direct traces of their mounting hardware.

REMOVAL PRIORITY:
The explicit REMOVE instructions take precedence over preserving
devices or objects attached to otherwise preserved surfaces.

Preserving a wall, ceiling, floor or cabinet does NOT mean preserving
the electrical devices, light fixtures or removable objects mounted on it.

RECONSTRUCT REMOVED AREAS:
Continue the existing walls, flooring, ceiling, baseboards and other
surfaces naturally behind every removed object.

Use the nearest visible surrounding surfaces as the reference for:
- Material and base color.
- Texture scale and direction.
- Perspective and geometry.
- Flooring patterns, joints and grout lines.
- Baseboard alignment.
- Natural daylight gradients.

Where the original surface was hidden, create a plausible,
conservative continuation of the existing finish.
Do not invent decorative features or new architectural elements.

Fill visible mounting holes and recesses left by removed items.
Do not leave object-shaped stains, silhouettes, blurred patches,
repeated texture artifacts or floating fragments.

EXPOSURE AND DAYLIGHT:
Preserve the direction and character of natural daylight entering
through the existing windows and openings.

Rebalance exposure as needed after removing artificial lighting.
The room must remain naturally readable without adding new lights.

Do not preserve artificial illumination merely to match the original
brightness. Remove fixture-generated hotspots and color casts.
Avoid blown-out windows, unnaturally dark corners and excessive HDR.

DO NOT:
- Add furniture, decor, appliances or replacement objects.
- Add new lighting fixtures, outlets, switches or visible wiring.
- Add or remove windows, doors or structural openings.
- Change the floor plan, room proportions or camera view.
- Change flooring, wall finishes or ceiling design.
- Add suspended ceilings, niches or panels to hide removed fixtures.
- Turn mirrors into architectural openings.
- Leave reflections, shadows or light halos from removed objects.
- Apply a new interior style or beautify the room.
- Blur the image to conceal incomplete removal.
